title: Missing time: waking up by a reservoir dam near Newell
place_text: Reservoir dam near Newell, South Dakota

tellings.quote: The truck is parked behind the wall of a reservoir dam near a town called Newell, more than 8 miles from their post.
I put the mike down and stepped out of the vehicle only to find that we were somewhere other than at November-5.
The sun was just coming up and I could see that it was a dam that held water in a reservoir. It turned out to be located north of Newell, and is called Newell Lake, quite a few miles from the LF.
During debriefing, I was told that nearly four hours had passed and that six security police back-up Alert teams had been searching for us.

plain: In 1977 two Air Force security policemen guarding a nuclear missile site in South Dakota, Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, say they found their truck parked behind a reservoir dam near the town of Newell, more than eight miles from their post, with hours they could not account for, which they take as a sign they were abducted. Michels retells it from the two men. An article by the journalist Robert Hastings, published in 2017, quotes the former guard: 'we were somewhere other than at November-5' (their missile launch site), the dam was 'called Newell Lake, quite a few miles' away, and at debriefing he 'was told that nearly four hours had passed and that six security police back-up Alert teams had been searching for us.'
